# Chemical coupling

The six-species comparison derives carbamate formation as R2 − R4 − R5 and
bicarbonate formation as R2 − R5. Their log equilibrium constants differ by
−ln K₄. Both net reactions share MEA, CO₂ and MEAH⁺, so carbon, amine and
charge balances couple their amounts. Activity coefficients also change with
the shared mixture composition.

The later reaction-temperature fit retained all five reactions and two SVD
directions. Those two directions reduce fitting freedom; they are not the two
net reactions. This distinction prevents a numerical rank statement from being
mistaken for a chemical species reduction.

# What has been tested

The staged work already tested neutral binary VLE, historical ionic/speciation parameter
regression, bounded CO₂/R4 calibration, dielectric formulations, reaction
temperature directions and paired heat. A detailed volumetric plan records 128
analog densities and 103 bulk MEA densities while keeping derived volumes
separate. It found no numerical exact aqueous MEAH⁺/MEACOO⁻ salt-density
evidence in the bounded search.

The July coupled designs specified joint pressure/speciation objectives,
frozen bounds, grouped partitions, multistart and identification requirements.
The 28 July shared-ion fit converged but worsened pressure; the August
pressure-first screen did not resolve the fit; Issue 70 retained a supported
negative decision. These results make the estimation strategy established
work, not an unresearched gap.

# Remaining identification boundary

The unresolved question is whether the carbamate/bicarbonate split can
separately identify reaction constants from ionic Born/dispersion and dielectric
effects under the exact model and data domain. The current reaction-temperature
fit held EOS parameters fixed and barely changed paired speciation RMSE
(0.3702 → 0.3670). The earlier ionic fit was not a joint identification study
of the current selection.

Before another fit, reconcile the reviewed evaluator correction and owner-held
F/S and ionic-screen results in the [scientific context map](https://github.com/tannerpolley/MEA-Thermodynamics/blob/codex/born-permittivity-formulation-study/docs/scientific/docs/scientific/CONTEXT.md)
and [September audit](https://github.com/tannerpolley/MEA-Thermodynamics/blob/codex/born-permittivity-formulation-study/docs/scientific/REPOSITORY_AUDIT_2026-09-08.md).
Do not treat a successful solve, a historical fit vector or a two-dimensional
sensitivity subspace as evidence of independent parameter identification.
